draft.title: Entwurf eines Gesetzes für ein steuerliches Investitionssofortprogramm zur Stärkung des Wirtschaftsstandorts Deutschland
draft.relevant_provision: Article 1 number 1, proposed §6(1) number4 EStG, physical/printed page 5; special electric-vehicle depreciation in Article 1 number 2(b), same page.
draft.version_check: The author expressly identifies BT 21/323. No later amendment or enacted version is substituted.
draft.bill_initiator: CDU/CSU and SPD parliamentary groups; Fraktionsgesetzentwurf, not the separately introduced government bill.

card.law_is_about: Tax changes intended to encourage business investment, including preferential treatment of electric business cars.
card.they_want: Oppose the specific preferential treatment of electric business cars.
card.they_claim: The passage contrasts an18% BEV new-registration share in May 2025 with a3.3% E-car share in2024.
card.the_problem: 3.3% is a fleet-stock share, while2024 BEV new registrations were13.5%. Whether the author intended a like-for-like comparison is unresolved.

claim_quote.translation_en: Translation of fragment: the share of electric passenger cars was only3.3 percent

counter_quote.original: 13,5 Prozent aller neu zugelassenen PKW wurden rein batterieelektrisch angetrieben.
counter_quote.translation_en: Translation:13.5 percent of all newly registered passenger cars were purely battery-electric.

correction: The contemporaneous March 2025 federal report gives13.5% for BEVs among2024 new registrations. The approximately3.3% figure corresponds to BEVs in the whole registered fleet at1January 2025. Fleet stock and new registrations have different denominators.
effect: If the passage intends a like-for-like change from2024 to May 2025, it greatly exaggerates the increase in new-registration share. That intended scope is not expressly stated.
limits: Unresolved, not a proved false value:3.3% is a valid approximate fleet-stock statistic, and the author does not expressly call it a new-registration share. The adjacent explanation invoking the May-only observation suggests comparison but could be imprecise contextual shorthand. The author also expressly lacks business-car demand and price-elasticity data. This does not prove or disprove the forecast tax-policy effect.
materiality_explanation: Minor if confirmed: the comparator concerns one piece of market context, while the anti-preference argument rests separately on CO2 pricing, targeting and fiscal concerns.
direction_explanation: Null: neither the intended2024 denominator nor a definite effect of this market-context comparison on the author’s request is established.
context_checks: Read all 13 pages and visually checked the complete passage on page 5 and the policy conclusion on page6.
The author immediately suggests May-only observation as a possible explanation; that is not a qualification distinguishing stock from new registrations.
The18% May 2025 figure is consistent with43,060 BEVs among239,297 new cars, and was not challenged.
The whole-fleet reading is a strong benign alternative and prevents promotion without further scope evidence.

history.event: Recorded as unresolved comparator lead; not treated as a proved false2024 value. Independent scope review requested.
Independent social-agent review retained the recorded classification after full source, exact bill and comparator checks.
